evidence.source: 蔡一峰, “古文字所謂「閒」「外」通諧說辨議”
evidence.text: The article reports 間 as a later variant spelling of 閒 and cites a Warring States bronze inscription (間右戈, 集成 10974) as an attestation. It cites late Western Zhou bronze examples of 閒, including 㝬鐘 (集成 260), whose graph places 月 outside 門. The author presents the traditional semantic interpretation as a gap at a door, with moonlight entering, and discusses a separate graph with an added 卜 as a Warring States differentiation of 閒. The paper also explains that scholars have proposed phonetic relations involving 月/外, but argues that the sound-series evidence is not secure and favors treating the series separately. This is a secondary paleographic study, not direct inspection of the cited bronzes.
evidence.title: 古文字所謂「閒」「外」通諧說辨議

evidence.source: 漢典 (ZDIC), quoting 說文解字 and 段玉裁注
evidence.field: 說文解字·閒; 說文解字注·閒
evidence.text: The entry says 說文 does not have 間 as its headword and directs readers to 閒: “隙也。从門从月” (a gap; from 門 and 月), with 古文 variants. The quoted 段注 expands the sense from a gap or interval between two sides to spaces, intervals in speech, and leisure; it describes 閒 as a semantic compound and repeats the traditional moonlight-through-a-door-gap account. These are historical lexicographic explanations, not independent proof of the graph’s creation circumstances.
evidence.title: 間 jiān、jiàn、jiǎn - 漢典

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The dictionary treats 閒 as a variant of 間 in later standardized usage. Its note quotes the tradition that 閒 was the earlier spelling for ‘gap/interval’, and that 間 became the conventional form for interval/between while 閒 was used especially for leisure; it also cites an epigraphic note that 閒 follows 月 in Shuowen and that the popular spelling uses 日. This supports the later spelling relation, but the entry does not establish the exact date or a single mechanism for every 日-form.
evidence.title: [A04378] 間 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Měng Péngshēng, Southwest University Institute for Chinese Language and Literature
evidence.text: In discussing Chu bamboo-slip material, the author cites Bao Shan slips 199 and 210 and interprets the written forms in context as 閒/間 ‘between, among’. This is an attestation in excavated Warring States manuscripts, though the paper’s reading is an editorial interpretation of the slip graphs and context.
evidence.kind: secondary scholarly study of excavated text
evidence.title: 孟蓬生 | 上博簡《艸茅之外(閒)》初讀

evidence.text: The entry cites 《禮記·樂記》 “一動一靜者，天地之閒也” for an interval/between sense, and cites older texts for separation, placing between, alternation, and a brief pause. It lists later examples for rooms, measure-word use, and extended senses. Because this is a dictionary’s collected citation list, it does not by itself date the semantic transitions or prove a linear chronology.
evidence.title: 間 jiān、jiàn、jiǎn - 漢典

evidence.text: For 間, the local table records Mandarin jiān, Middle Chinese kean, and Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *kˤre[n] for ‘interval’ and a separate chariot-linchpin sound gloss. A different row gives 間 xián, Middle Chinese hean, Old Chinese *N-kˤre[n] for ‘idle’. The table has no 閒 row, so it cannot independently verify a proposed component-to-host sound comparison with 閒.

evidence.source: Wiktionary, 閒 entry, reflecting cited historical phonology references
evidence.text: The entry reports Baxter–Sagart *N-kˤre[n] and Zhengzhang *ɡreːn for an 閒 reading ‘idle’, and gives other proposed relationships, including connection to 間 in some scholarship and a Tai-language loan proposal in Schuessler. These are competing word-etymology analyses; they do not establish that 月 functions as a phonetic component in 閒, nor do they establish sound-component status for 日 in 間. The local Baxter–Sagart table has no 閒 row, so its notation is not locally cross-checked.

evidence.text: The file page identifies 閒-bronze-warring.svg as a modern Inkscape drawing of 閒 in Warring States bronze-script style. It names the source glyph as Xiaoxuetang record 33.EEC1, associated with the late Warring States 兆域圖銅版 (集成 10478), and marks the representation CC0/public domain. This is a redraw, not a photograph of the bronze.

gaps: The inspected evidence does not establish an oracle-bone attestation for 間/閒; the earliest securely dated examples reported here are late Western Zhou bronze for 閒 and Warring States evidence for 間.

No direct image of any inscription or slip was visually examined. The paleographic paper reports and interprets those forms; ZDIC’s glyph samples are not enough to establish each graphic stage independently.

The traditional 門+月 moonlight explanation is a historical account and a plausible semantic interpretation. The dossier’s 門+日 sunlight version is repeated in secondary summaries, but the inspected sources do not establish its earliest instance or prove that it originated independently rather than as a graphic/spelling replacement.

The local Baxter–Sagart TSV contains multiple 間 readings but no 閒 row; no equivalent system-aligned host/component reconstruction comparison can be made from the local dataset. Do not treat 閒’s proposed historical relation to 間 as a demonstrated phonetic-component analysis.

Unihan records for 間 and 閒 were not accessible through the official character lookup URLs in this session. 間’s local kMandarin row is jiān, but it is not emitted as externally verified evidence. The local tracked HSK extract has no covered rows for these characters.

The sources document semantic range and examples but do not establish a dated sequence for every extension, including ‘space/place’, ‘room’, measure-word, interval in time, leisure, and separating/interposing uses. Separate lexical histories and divergent readings may be involved.

No independently established source-word/original-object borrowing claim was identified for this character; the chariot-linchpin sound gloss appears in the local historical-phonology data but was not externally researched as an object-name borrowing claim.

No image is proposed: although Commons search results supplied a relevant redraw and provenance, the candidate Commons file page could not be opened in the browser, so an actual direct image URL and independently inspectable reuse terms were not verified. Xiaoxuetang character-specific records and its rights notice also could not be inspected. The Commons result states CC0/public-domain terms, but under this stage's requirements that result alone is insufficient to select an asset.
